description:
About the Scholarships

Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich, one of Germany’s leading research universities, coordinates a group of scholarships for international students enrolled (or about to enrol) in LMU degree programmes. The schemes — which include foundation and university-funded awards — exist because of a specific German reality: public-university tuition is largely free, so the real financial barrier for international students is the cost of living in one of Germany’s most expensive cities. The awards therefore pay a monthly maintenance contribution rather than a tuition waiver. A single application between 15 January and 8 March puts you forward for every scheme you qualify for, which keeps the process unusually simple for a German university.

What the Funding Covers

The awards pay a monthly amount towards rent, food, health insurance and study materials — the everyday costs that add up in Munich. Amounts vary by scheme and are typically in the range associated with German foundation scholarships; they are contributions, not full cost-of-living coverage, so most recipients combine them with part-time work, family support or other funding. Since LMU charges no conventional tuition for most programmes, a maintenance award goes further in Germany than an equivalent grant almost anywhere else. Awards are generally granted for a defined period and can be extended subject to study progress.

Eligibility Criteria

  • International (non-German) students enrolled in an LMU degree programme or doctoral research.
  • Strong academic record — the schemes are merit-based, with financial circumstances also considered.
  • Applicants must not hold comparable funding from another major German scholarship provider.
  • Application documents typically include proof of enrollment, transcripts, CV, motivation letter and income details.
  • German or English proficiency depending on your programme of study.

How to Apply

Applications open each year on 15 January and close on 8 March. Prepare the standard document set — enrollment certificate, academic transcripts, CV, a short motivation statement and evidence of your financial situation — and submit everything through the LMU portal or by post as instructed on the official page. Because one application covers all matching schemes, precision matters: state clearly which degree programme you are in and your intended funding period. Incomplete files are the most common reason applications are set aside, so check the published application-requirements PDF before submitting.

Important Notes

Munich’s rental market is tight, and scholarship payments arrive only after the semester starts — arrive with a financial buffer for the first two months. Applicants who miss the March window usually have to wait a full year, as the cycle runs annually. LMU’s International Office also lists external German foundations (political, religious and business-affiliated) that fund internationals; applying to those in parallel significantly raises your overall odds.
